Ed Shaughnessy may be the most recognized drummer in the country. His dynamic playing and vivacious personality have sparked the bands of Jack Teagarden, Benny Goodman, Duke Ellington and George Shearing. A native of Jersey City, Ed’s first playing experience was in the clubs of the flourishing jazz scene on New York’s 52nd Street. In the 50’s he was kept busy in the studios and as a staff drummer with CBS television. As the Tonight Show drummer, Ed became a familiar face with nation-wide audiences and moved to Los Angeles with the show in 1972. When the Basie Band was in need of a drummer for recording, the Count would call on Ed and referred to him as his “Secret Weapon.” He has recorded with jazz greats Oliver Nelson, Quincy Jones, Zoot Sims and Wes Montgomery. Ed is currently in demand at schools and colleges across the country and frequently appears at festivals and jazz parties throughout the world.
Ed was interviewed in Clinton, New York on April 25, 1998 by Monk Rowe, director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
We are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive on the Hamilton campus today. It’s an extreme pleasure for me to welcome Ed Shaughnessy for actually Part Two of our interview series.
No I just need another helping. It’s been like two years, or three.
I think it might be three. Yeah.
